# google_compute_ha_controller

Represents an HA Controller resource.

## Example Usage - Compute Ha Controller Basic


```hcl
locals {
  region = "us-central1"
  zone1  = "us-central1-a"
  zone2  = "us-central1-b"
}

data "google_compute_image" "debian_13" {
  family  = "debian-13"
  project = "debian-cloud"
}

resource "google_compute_region_disk" "regional_disk" {
  name                      = "hac-bs-rd"
  physical_block_size_bytes = 4096
  type                      = "pd-balanced"
  region                    = local.region
  replica_zones             = [local.zone1, local.zone2]
  size                      = 10
  image                     = data.google_compute_image.debian_13.self_link
}

resource "google_compute_instance" "vm" {
  name         = "hac-bs-inst"
  machine_type = "e2-micro"
  zones {
    zone = local.zone1
  }
  zones {
    zone = local.zone2
  }

  boot_disk {
    auto_delete = false
    source      = google_compute_region_disk.regional_disk.self_link
  }

  network_interface {
    network = "default"
  }

  allow_stopping_for_update = true
}

resource "google_compute_ha_controller" "ha_controller" {
  name                = "hac-bs"
  region              = local.region
  instance_name       = google_compute_instance.vm.name
  failover_initiation = "MANUAL_ONLY"

  zone_configuration {
    zone = local.zone1
  }
  zone_configuration {
    zone = local.zone2
  }

  # To recreate the VMs, Compute Engine must delete the HA Controller first.
  lifecycle {
    replace_triggered_by = [
      google_compute_instance.vm.id
    ]
  }
}
```

## Example Usage - Compute Ha Controller Reservations


```hcl
locals {
  region = "us-central1"
  zone1  = "us-central1-a"
  zone2  = "us-central1-b"
}

data "google_compute_image" "debian_13" {
  family  = "debian-13"
  project = "debian-cloud"
}

resource "google_compute_region_disk" "regional_disk" {
  name                      = "hac-rv-rd"
  physical_block_size_bytes = 4096
  type                      = "pd-balanced"
  region                    = local.region
  replica_zones             = [local.zone1, local.zone2]
  size                      = 10
  image                     = data.google_compute_image.debian_13.self_link
}

# Reservations in both zones must have the same name; otherwise, you encounter
# errors after a failover because the Terraform state no longer matches your
# configuration.
resource "google_compute_reservation" "reservation_zone1" {
  name = "hac-rv-rv" # same name as in zone 2
  zone = local.zone1

  specific_reservation {
    count = 1
    instance_properties {
      machine_type = "e2-micro"
    }
  }

  reservation_sharing_policy {
    service_share_type = "DISALLOW_ALL"
  }

  specific_reservation_required = true
}

resource "google_compute_reservation" "reservation_zone2" {
  name = "hac-rv-rv" # same name as in zone 1
  zone = local.zone2

  specific_reservation {
    count = 1
    instance_properties {
      machine_type = "e2-micro"
    }
  }

  reservation_sharing_policy {
    service_share_type = "DISALLOW_ALL"
  }

  specific_reservation_required = true
}

resource "google_compute_instance" "vm" {
  name         = "hac-rv-inst"
  machine_type = "e2-micro"
  zones {
    zone = local.zone1
  }
  zones {
    zone = local.zone2
  }

  boot_disk {
    auto_delete = false
    source      = google_compute_region_disk.regional_disk.self_link
  }

  network_interface {
    subnetwork = "default"
    stack_type = "IPV4_ONLY"
  }

  reservation_affinity {
    type = "SPECIFIC_RESERVATION"
    specific_reservation {
      key    = "compute.googleapis.com/reservation-name"
      values = [google_compute_reservation.reservation_zone1.name]
    }
  }

  allow_stopping_for_update = true
}

resource "google_compute_ha_controller" "ha_controller" {
  name                = "hac-rv"
  region              = local.region
  instance_name       = google_compute_instance.vm.name
  failover_initiation = "MANUAL_ONLY"

  networking_auto_configuration {
    internal {
      stack_type = "IPV4_ONLY"
    }
  }

  # Reservations in both zones must have the same name; otherwise, you encounter
  # errors after a failover because the Terraform state no longer matches your
  # configuration.
  zone_configuration {
    zone = local.zone1
    reservation_affinity {
      type = "SPECIFIC_RESERVATION"
      specific_reservation {
        key    = "compute.googleapis.com/reservation-name"
        values = [google_compute_reservation.reservation_zone1.name]
      }
    }
  }
  zone_configuration {
    zone = local.zone2
    reservation_affinity {
      type = "SPECIFIC_RESERVATION"
      specific_reservation {
        key    = "compute.googleapis.com/reservation-name"
        values = [google_compute_reservation.reservation_zone2.name]
      }
    }
  }

  # To recreate the VMs, Compute Engine must delete the HA Controller first.
  lifecycle {
    replace_triggered_by = [
      google_compute_instance.vm.id
    ]
  }
}
```

## Example Usage - Compute Ha Controller Sole Tenancy


```hcl
locals {
  region = "us-central1"
  zone1  = "us-central1-a"
  zone2  = "us-central1-b"
}

data "google_compute_image" "debian_13" {
  family  = "debian-13"
  project = "debian-cloud"
}

resource "google_compute_region_disk" "regional_disk" {
  name                      = "hac-st-rd"
  physical_block_size_bytes = 4096
  type                      = "pd-balanced"
  region                    = local.region
  replica_zones             = [local.zone1, local.zone2]
  size                      = 10
  image                     = data.google_compute_image.debian_13.self_link
}

resource "google_compute_node_template" "node_template1" {
  name      = "hac-st-ntmpl"
  region    = local.region
  node_type = "n1-node-96-624"
  node_affinity_labels = {
    workload = "synthetic"
    distinct = "1"
  }
}

resource "google_compute_node_template" "node_template2" {
  name      = "hac-st-ntmpl2"
  region    = local.region
  node_type = "n1-node-96-624"
  node_affinity_labels = {
    workload = "synthetic"
    distinct = "2"
  }
}

resource "google_compute_node_group" "sole_tenant_group1" {
  name          = "hac-st-stgrp1"
  zone          = local.zone1
  node_template = google_compute_node_template.node_template1.id
  initial_size  = 1
}

resource "google_compute_node_group" "sole_tenant_group2" {
  name          = "hac-st-stgrp2"
  zone          = local.zone2
  node_template = google_compute_node_template.node_template2.id
  initial_size  = 1
}

resource "google_compute_instance" "vm" {
  name         = "hac-st-inst"
  machine_type = "n1-standard-1"
  zones {
    zone = local.zone1
  }
  zones {
    zone = local.zone2
  }

  depends_on = [
    google_compute_node_group.sole_tenant_group1,
    google_compute_node_group.sole_tenant_group2,
  ]

  boot_disk {
    auto_delete = false
    source      = google_compute_region_disk.regional_disk.self_link
  }

  network_interface {
    subnetwork = "default"
    stack_type = "IPV4_ONLY"
  }

  scheduling {
    node_affinities {
      key      = "workload"
      operator = "IN"
      values   = ["synthetic"]
    }
  }

  allow_stopping_for_update = true
}

resource "google_compute_ha_controller" "ha_controller" {
  name                = "hac-st"
  region              = local.region
  instance_name       = google_compute_instance.vm.name
  failover_initiation = "MANUAL_ONLY"

  zone_configuration {
    zone = local.zone1
    node_affinities {
      key      = "workload"
      operator = "IN"
      values   = ["synthetic"]
    }
  }
  zone_configuration {
    zone = local.zone2
    node_affinities {
      key      = "workload"
      operator = "IN"
      values   = ["synthetic"]
    }
  }

  # To recreate the VMs, Compute Engine must delete the HA Controller first.
  lifecycle {
    replace_triggered_by = [
      google_compute_instance.vm.id
    ]
  }
}
```

## Example Usage - Compute Ha Controller Backend Service


```hcl
locals {
  region  = "us-central1"
  zone1   = "us-central1-a"
  zone2   = "us-central1-b"
  network = "default"
}

data "google_compute_image" "debian_13" {
  family  = "debian-13"
  project = "debian-cloud"
}

resource "google_compute_region_disk" "regional_disk" {
  name                      = "hac-rbs-rd"
  physical_block_size_bytes = 4096
  type                      = "pd-balanced"
  region                    = local.region
  replica_zones             = [local.zone1, local.zone2]
  size                      = 10
  image                     = data.google_compute_image.debian_13.self_link
}

resource "google_compute_instance" "vm" {
  name         = "hac-rbs-inst"
  machine_type = "e2-micro"
  zones {
    zone = local.zone1
  }
  zones {
    zone = local.zone2
  }

  boot_disk {
    auto_delete = false
    source      = google_compute_region_disk.regional_disk.self_link
  }

  network_interface {
    network = local.network
  }

  allow_stopping_for_update = true
}

resource "google_compute_region_backend_service" "backend_service" {
  name                  = "hac-rbs-bs"
  region                = local.region
  protocol              = "UNSPECIFIED"
  load_balancing_scheme = "INTERNAL"
  network               = local.network

  ha_policy {
    fast_ip_move = "DISABLED"
  }

  connection_draining_timeout_sec = 0
}

resource "google_compute_ha_controller" "ha_controller" {
  name                = "hac-rbs"
  region              = local.region
  instance_name       = google_compute_instance.vm.name
  failover_initiation = "MANUAL_ONLY"

  backend_services = [google_compute_region_backend_service.backend_service.self_link]

  zone_configuration {
    zone = local.zone1
  }
  zone_configuration {
    zone = local.zone2
  }

  # To recreate the VMs, Compute Engine must delete the HA Controller first.
  lifecycle {
    replace_triggered_by = [
      google_compute_instance.vm.id
    ]
  }
}
```

## Example Usage - Compute Ha Controller Multi Nic Static Ip


```hcl
locals {
  region = "us-central1"
  zone1  = "us-central1-a"
  zone2  = "us-central1-b"
}

data "google_compute_image" "debian_13" {
  family  = "debian-13"
  project = "debian-cloud"
}

data "google_compute_network" "net_0" {
  name = "hac-sip-net0"
}

resource "google_compute_subnetwork" "subnet_0" {
  name          = "hac-sip-sub0"
  ip_cidr_range = "10.0.1.0/24"
  region        = local.region
  network       = data.google_compute_network.net_0.id
}

data "google_compute_network" "net_1" {
  name = "hac-sip-net1"
}

resource "google_compute_subnetwork" "subnet_1" {
  name          = "hac-sip-sub1"
  ip_cidr_range = "10.0.2.0/24"
  region        = local.region
  network       = data.google_compute_network.net_1.id
}

resource "google_compute_address" "ipv4_nic0_zone1" {
  name         = "hac-sip-v4-n0-z1"
  region       = local.region
  subnetwork   = google_compute_subnetwork.subnet_0.id
  address_type = "INTERNAL"
  address      = "10.0.1.10"
}

resource "google_compute_address" "ipv4_nic0_zone2" {
  name         = "hac-sip-v4-n0-z2"
  region       = local.region
  subnetwork   = google_compute_subnetwork.subnet_0.id
  address_type = "INTERNAL"
  address      = "10.0.1.11"
}

resource "google_compute_address" "ipv4_nic1_zone1" {
  name         = "hac-sip-v4-n1-z1"
  region       = local.region
  subnetwork   = google_compute_subnetwork.subnet_1.id
  address_type = "INTERNAL"
  address      = "10.0.2.10"
}

resource "google_compute_address" "ipv4_nic1_zone2" {
  name         = "hac-sip-v4-n1-z2"
  region       = local.region
  subnetwork   = google_compute_subnetwork.subnet_1.id
  address_type = "INTERNAL"
  address      = "10.0.2.11"
}

resource "google_compute_region_disk" "regional_disk" {
  name                      = "hac-sip-rd"
  physical_block_size_bytes = 4096
  type                      = "pd-balanced"
  region                    = local.region
  replica_zones             = [local.zone1, local.zone2]
  size                      = 10
  image                     = data.google_compute_image.debian_13.self_link
}

resource "google_compute_instance" "vm" {
  name         = "hac-sip-inst"
  machine_type = "e2-micro"
  zones {
    zone = local.zone1
    network_interface {
      name       = "nic0"
      network_ip = google_compute_address.ipv4_nic0_zone1.address
    }
    network_interface {
      name       = "nic1"
      network_ip = google_compute_address.ipv4_nic1_zone1.address
    }
  }
  zones {
    zone = local.zone2
    network_interface {
      name       = "nic0"
      network_ip = google_compute_address.ipv4_nic0_zone2.address
    }
    network_interface {
      name       = "nic1"
      network_ip = google_compute_address.ipv4_nic1_zone2.address
    }
  }

  boot_disk {
    auto_delete = false
    source      = google_compute_region_disk.regional_disk.self_link
  }

  network_interface {
    subnetwork = google_compute_subnetwork.subnet_0.self_link
  }

  network_interface {
    subnetwork = google_compute_subnetwork.subnet_1.self_link
  }

  allow_stopping_for_update = true
}

resource "google_compute_ha_controller" "ha_controller" {
  name                = "hac-sip"
  region              = local.region
  instance_name       = google_compute_instance.vm.name
  failover_initiation = "MANUAL_ONLY"

  zone_configuration {
    zone = local.zone1
    instance_network_interface {
      name       = "nic0"
      network_ip = google_compute_address.ipv4_nic0_zone1.address
    }
    instance_network_interface {
      name       = "nic1"
      network_ip = google_compute_address.ipv4_nic1_zone1.address
    }
  }
  zone_configuration {
    zone = local.zone2
    instance_network_interface {
      name       = "nic0"
      network_ip = google_compute_address.ipv4_nic0_zone2.address
    }
    instance_network_interface {
      name       = "nic1"
      network_ip = google_compute_address.ipv4_nic1_zone2.address
    }
  }

  # To recreate the VMs, Compute Engine must delete the HA Controller first.
  lifecycle {
    replace_triggered_by = [
      google_compute_instance.vm.id
    ]
  }
}
```

## Argument Reference

The following arguments are supported:


* `name` -
  (Required)
  The name for the resource.
  The name must be 1-63 characters long and comply with RFC1035.

* `instance_name` -
  (Required)
  The name of the instance that the HA Controller manages.
  The name must comply with RFC1035.
  The instance must exist in one of the two zones specified in the zone_configuration block.

* `zone_configuration` -
  (Required)
  A set of exactly two distinct zone configurations.
  Structure is [documented below](#nested_zone_configuration).


* `description` -
  (Optional)
  A description of this resource.
  Maximum length of 2048 characters.

* `failover_initiation` -
  (Optional)
  Specifies how to initiate failover. Valid values are the following:
  * `AUTOMATIC`: Automatically detects zonal outages and performs failover.
  * `MANUAL_ONLY`: Requires you to manually initiate failover.

* `networking_auto_configuration` -
  (Optional)
  Basic networking configuration. Required backend services and
  forwarding rules will be automatically created with default parameters.
  Structure is [documented below](#nested_networking_auto_configuration).

* `backend_services` -
  (Optional)
  The full URL of the backend service.
  Currently, you can specify only one backend service,
  and it must be an L4 Internal Load Balancer (ILB).

* `region` -
  (Optional)
  The region where the HA Controller will be created.

* `project` - (Optional) The ID of the project in which the resource belongs.
    If it is not provided, the provider project is used.

* `deletion_policy` - (Optional) Whether Terraform will be prevented from destroying the resource. Defaults to DELETE.
	When a 'terraform destroy' or 'terraform apply' would delete the resource,
	the command will fail if this field is set to "PREVENT" in Terraform state.
	When set to "ABANDON", the command will remove the resource from Terraform
	management without updating or deleting the resource in the API.
	When set to "DELETE", deleting the resource is allowed.


<a name="nested_zone_configuration"></a>The `zone_configuration` block supports:

* `zone` -
  (Required)
  The name of the zone. The zone must be unique for each block.

* `reservation_affinity` -
  (Optional)
  A nested object resource.
  Structure is [documented below](#nested_zone_configuration_reservation_affinity).

* `node_affinities` -
  (Optional)
  Specifies node affinities or anti-affinities to determine
  which sole-tenant nodes your instances and managed instance groups (MIGs) use
  as host systems.
  Structure is [documented below](#nested_zone_configuration_node_affinities).

* `instance_network_interface` -
  (Optional)
  The network interface configuration of a VM instance in this zone.
  Maximum of 8 network interfaces can be specified.
  Structure is [documented below](#nested_zone_configuration_instance_network_interface).


<a name="nested_zone_configuration_reservation_affinity"></a>The `reservation_affinity` block supports:

* `type` -
  (Optional)
  Specifies the type of reservation from which this instance can consume resources. Possible values:
  - `NO_RESERVATION`: The instance doesn't consume any reservations, even if existing, matching reservations have capacity available.
  - `ANY_RESERVATION`: The instance automatically consumes any reservation with matching properties.
  - `SPECIFIC_RESERVATION`: The instance consumes a specific, matching reservation. You must also provide key and values to consume the reservation. Otherwise, you encounter errors.

* `specific_reservation` -
  (Optional)
  Required when type is SPECIFIC_RESERVATION
  Structure is [documented below](#nested_zone_configuration_reservation_affinity_specific_reservation).


<a name="nested_zone_configuration_reservation_affinity_specific_reservation"></a>The `specific_reservation` block supports:

* `key` -
  (Optional)
  The key for the reservation. To target a SPECIFIC_RESERVATION by name,
  use "compute.googleapis.com/reservation-name".

* `values` -
  (Optional)
  The values for the reservation. Typically the name of the reservation.
  For shared reservations, use the format
  "projects/different-project/reservations/some-reservation-name".
  Limited to a single value.

<a name="nested_zone_configuration_node_affinities"></a>The `node_affinities` block supports:

* `key` -
  (Required)
  The key for the node affinity label.

* `operator` -
  (Required)
  Defines the operation of node selection.
  Possible values:
  - `IN`: Requires Compute Engine to seek for matched nodes.
  - `NOT_IN`: Requires Compute Engine to avoid certain nodes.

* `values` -
  (Required)
  Corresponds to the label values of Node resource.

<a name="nested_zone_configuration_instance_network_interface"></a>The `instance_network_interface` block supports:

* `name` -
  (Optional)
  The name of the network interface. A VM network interface uses the `nicN`
  naming format, where `N` is a value between `0` and `7`. The default
  interface is `nic0`.

* `network_ip` -
  (Optional)
  The internal IPv4 address to assign to the instance's network interface
  when the instance is in this zone. If you don't specify an address,
  then Google Cloud assigns an ephemeral IPv4 address based on the stack type
  of the network interface.

* `ipv6_address` -
  (Optional)
  The internal IPv6 address to assign to the instance's network interface
  when the instance is in this zone. If you don't specify an address, then
  Google Cloud assigns an ephemeral IPv6 address based on the stack type of
  the network interface.

<a name="nested_networking_auto_configuration"></a>The `networking_auto_configuration` block supports:

* `internal` -
  (Optional)
  Internal networking configuration.
  Structure is [documented below](#nested_networking_auto_configuration_internal).


<a name="nested_networking_auto_configuration_internal"></a>The `internal` block supports:

* `stack_type` -
  (Optional)
  Determine which IP addresses to automatically create.
  Possible values:
  - `IPV4_ONLY`: Assign IPv4 address only.
  - `IPV4_IPV6`: Assign both IPv4 and IPv6 addresses.
  - `IPV6_ONLY`: Assign IPv6 address only.

* `ip_address` -
  (Optional)
  The IP address. If you don't provide this value,
  then Terraform automatically allocates the IP address based on
  the stack_type.

* `ipv6_address` -
  (Optional)
  The IPv6 address. If you don't provide this value,
  then Terraform automatically allocates the IPv6 address based on
  the stack_type.

## Attributes Reference

In addition to the arguments listed above, the following computed attributes are exported:

* `id` - an identifier for the resource with format `projects/{{project}}/regions/{{region}}/haControllers/{{name}}`

* `creation_timestamp` -
  The creation timestamp for the HA Controller in RFC3339 text format.

* `self_link_with_id` -
  The server-defined URL for the HA Controller. This URL includes the resource ID.

* `state` -
  The current state of the HA Controller.
  Possible values are the following:
  - `ACTIVE`: The HA Controller is active and ready to fail over the instance.
  - `CREATING`: Compute Engine is creating the HA Controller.
  - `DELETING`: Compute Engine is deleting the HA Controller.
  - `FAILOVER_IN_PROGRESS`: The HA Controller is failing over the instance to the secondary zone.
  - `FAILOVER_UNAVAILABLE`: The HA Controller isn't ready to fail over the instance.
  - `MULTI_ZONE_FAILURE`: The instance requires a failover, but the secondary zone isn't available.
  - `PENDING_FAILOVER`: The instance requires a failover.
  - `STARTING`: Compute Engine is starting the HA Controller.
  - `STOPPED`: The HA Controller is stopped.
  - `STOPPING`: Compute Engine is stopping the HA Controller.
  - `UPDATING`: Compute Engine is updating the HA Controller.

* `status` -
  The current status of the HA Controller.
  Structure is [documented below](#nested_status).
* `self_link` - The URI of the created resource.


<a name="nested_status"></a>The `status` block contains:

* `primary_zone` -
  (Output)
  The name of the primary zone for the instance. Compute Engine updates this field at the
  start of a failover operation, so this zone might not be operational during a failover.

* `primary_instance` -
  (Output)
  The URL of the instance in the primary zone. Compute Engine updates this field at the
  start of a failover operation.

* `ongoing_failover` -
  (Output)
  Indicates whether a failover operation is in progress.

* `ready_for_failover` -
  (Output)
  Indicates whether the HA Controller is ready to fail over the instance to the secondary zone.

* `zone_status` -
  (Output)
  A map that contains the status of each configured zone, where each key is the name of the zone.
  Structure is [documented below](#nested_status_zone_status).


<a name="nested_status_zone_status"></a>The `zone_status` block contains:

* `zone` - (Required) The identifier for this object. Format specified above.

* `is_primary` -
  (Output)
  Indicates whether this zone is the primary zone.

* `is_zone_ready` -
  (Output)
  Indicates whether this zone is ready for a failover.

## Timeouts

This resource provides the following
[Timeouts](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/plugin/sdkv2/resources/retries-and-customizable-timeouts) configuration options:

- `create` - Default is 20 minutes.
- `update` - Default is 20 minutes.
- `delete` - Default is 20 minutes.

## Import


HaController can be imported using any of these accepted formats:

* `projects/{{project}}/regions/{{region}}/haControllers/{{name}}`
* `{{project}}/{{region}}/{{name}}`
* `{{region}}/{{name}}`
* `{{name}}`

In Terraform v1.12.0 and later, use an [`identity` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/block/import#identity) to import HaController using identity values. For example:

```tf
import {
  identity = {
    name = "<-required value->"
    region = "<-optional value->"
    project = "<-optional value->"
  }
  to = google_compute_ha_controller.default
}
```

In Terraform v1.5.0 and later, use an [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) to import HaController using one of the formats above. For example:

```tf
import {
  id = "projects/{{project}}/regions/{{region}}/haControllers/{{name}}"
  to = google_compute_ha_controller.default
}
```

When using the [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import), HaController can be imported using one of the formats above. For example:

```
$ terraform import google_compute_ha_controller.default projects/{{project}}/regions/{{region}}/haControllers/{{name}}
$ terraform import google_compute_ha_controller.default {{project}}/{{region}}/{{name}}
$ terraform import google_compute_ha_controller.default {{region}}/{{name}}
$ terraform import google_compute_ha_controller.default {{name}}
```

## User Project Overrides

This resource supports [User Project Overrides](https://registry.terraform.io/providers/hashicorp/google/latest/docs/guides/provider_reference#user_project_override).
